title: a foreign property reached through an index signature needs an annotated adapter whether it is spelled with a dot or with an element access
notes:
specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary' (Locked): 'Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration.' A getter reached through an index signature is such a call. THE DELIBERATE PAIR of 09-foreign-calls/a-foreign-index-signature-read-through-a-property-access-needs-an-adapter: the same read off the same value, `keyed["width"]` here against `keyed.width` there. Two cases rather than one because the rule under test is that the refusal follows the RECEIVER's provenance and not the spelling: a rule keyed on `ts.PropertyAccessExpression` refuses the dotted case and admits this one, and the pair is the only thing that can see the difference. The declared VIBE1101 at the function declaration is the same row charge every other foreign read in this area declares, and it is why this case carries an xfail for `go`.

2026-09-07 retirement: measured as XPASS in the full native-only corpus run. The native boundary reporter now charges Panic to the enclosing row before inference, so both profiles report the complete authored diagnostic list, including VIBE1101. No source, required code, position or message assertion was removed.
